architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created a new top-level documentation page 'editor-support.md' instead of nesting it under existing sections like 'how-to' or 'advanced'
architecture_decisions.rationale: The VS Code extension is a significant development tool that deserves its own dedicated section rather than being buried in existing categories. This makes it easily discoverable and gives it appropriate prominence alongside other major topics like 'fastapi-cli' and 'Deployment'.
alternatives_considered: Adding it as a subsection under 'how-to' or 'advanced' sections
Embedding the content directly in the tutorial without a dedicated page

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added a contextual tip in the tutorial index page to promote the extension at the optimal learning moment
architecture_decisions.rationale: The tutorial index is where users begin their FastAPI journey. Adding the tip after installation instructions but before the advanced guide ensures users discover the extension early when they're setting up their development environment, maximizing adoption.
alternatives_considered: Adding the tip at the very beginning of the tutorial
Creating a separate 'getting started' section for editor tools
Only linking from the navigation without in-content promotion

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Placed the editor support page in the main navigation between 'fastapi-cli.md' and 'Deployment' sections
architecture_decisions.rationale: This positioning groups development tools together (CLI and editor extension) while maintaining logical flow from development tools to deployment. It creates a natural progression: CLI tools → Editor support → Deployment options.
alternatives_considered: Placing it at the end of the navigation
Creating a new 'Tools' section grouping CLI and editor support
Adding it to the beginning of the navigation as a 'Getting Started' item

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Structured the editor support page with clear sections: overview, setup/installation, application discovery, and features
architecture_decisions.rationale: This hierarchical structure follows the same pattern as other FastAPI documentation: starting with high-level overview, then practical setup instructions, configuration details, and finally feature explanations. This familiar structure helps users quickly find the information they need.
alternatives_considered: A single continuous page without sections
Separating setup and features into different pages
Organizing by editor type (VS Code vs Cursor) rather than by topic

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Used external links to marketplace, GitHub repository, and FastAPI Cloud while maintaining the FastAPI documentation style
architecture_decisions.rationale: The extension exists outside the core FastAPI repository, so linking to external resources is necessary. Using the existing 'external-link' CSS class ensures consistent styling with other external links in the documentation while clearly indicating these are external resources.
alternatives_considered: Using iframes or embedded content from external sources
Creating a separate microsite for extension documentation

implementation_summary:
The implementation follows a three-pronged approach to integrate VS Code extension documentation into the FastAPI ecosystem. First, a dedicated 'editor-support.md' page was created with comprehensive documentation structured similarly to other FastAPI documentation pages, featuring clear sections for overview, setup, configuration, and features. This maintains consistency with existing documentation patterns while providing complete information in one location.

Second, strategic promotion was added to the tutorial index page as a tip box placed after installation instructions but before the advanced guide. This timing is crucial - users discover the extension just as they're setting up their development environment, maximizing the likelihood of adoption. The tip uses the same 'external-link' styling as other external resources in the documentation.

Third, the navigation was updated in 'mkdocs.yml' to include the new page between 'fastapi-cli.md' and the 'Deployment' section. This positioning groups development tools together while maintaining a logical flow from development to deployment. The implementation respects the existing documentation architecture by adding a new top-level page rather than forcing it into existing categories, giving the extension appropriate prominence as a major development tool.

All changes maintain the existing FastAPI documentation conventions, including external link styling, section headers with anchor IDs, and the use of definition tags (<dfn>) for consistent terminology. The approach balances completeness (full documentation page) with discoverability (strategic tutorial promotion) while integrating seamlessly into the existing documentation structure.
